[← Telecom](../index.qmd)

The measurements and calculations behind every coverage and quality decision: what RSRP, RSRQ and SINR really mean, why the uplink usually decides coverage, how to build a link budget, how bands differ, and a method for reading drive tests. Six sections, each from the basic idea to field practice.

## Sections

::: {.lesson-table .column-page}
| | Section | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [What RSRP Really Measures](lectures/01-what-rsrp-measures.qmd) | RSRP as power per resource element; why it reads −95 dBm when the analyzer shows −60 dBm; reporting ranges; per-beam RSRP; RSRP in cell selection |
| 2 | [RSRQ, SINR & Drive Tests](lectures/02-rsrq-sinr-drive-tests.qmd) | Loud vs clear: RSRQ and SINR; why RSRQ depends on load; why SS-SINR can look worse than real traffic SINR; predicting SINR from RSRPs; pilot pollution |
| 3 | [The Uplink Bottleneck](lectures/03-uplink-bottleneck.qmd) | Why the phone's 0.2 W limits coverage; the DL/UL asymmetry in RSRP terms; uplink power control (P0, α, TPC); power headroom; ways to rescue the uplink |
| 4 | [Link Budget on a Napkin](lectures/04-link-budget.qmd) | The link budget as income and expenses; noise floor and sensitivity; margins; maximum allowed path loss; from path loss to distance with TR 38.901; building penetration |
| 5 | [700 MHz vs 3.5 GHz vs 28 GHz](lectures/05-bands-700-3500-28000.qmd) | Low, mid and high bands; free-space loss vs frequency; wavelength and antenna size; building penetration; the role of each layer |
| 6 | [Reading a Drive Test](lectures/06-reading-a-drive-test.qmd) | A step-by-step method for drive-test analysis; symptom-to-cause table; measurement filtering; events A1–A6; handover failures (too late, too early, ping-pong) |
:::

## How each section works

Every section climbs in three steps, so you can stop where you need to:

1. **Beginner · the idea**: what it is and why it matters, in plain words.
2. **Intermediate · how it works**: the mechanism, with the key numbers.
3. **Advanced · expert depth**: equations, 3GPP clauses and field practice.

Then a short **Practice** slide with exercises (answers in the speaker
notes, press **S**) and the references.

**Previous:** [Chapter 2 · Finding the Network](../ch2-finding-the-network/index.qmd) · **Next:** [Chapter 4 · Beams, Antennas & Hardware](../ch4-beams-antennas-hardware/index.qmd)
